blocks.title: Singleton pattern
blocks.text: The Singleton design pattern makes sure that a specific object or resource is created only once in a program and is reused whenever it is needed.
Think of it like having just one key to a special room: no matter who needs to get in, they all use that same key. No new keys are made, and everyone shares the one key.

blocks.prompt: Give a software example where only one object of a kind should exist.
blocks.explanation: For example the single settings (configuration) object of an application, or one shared connection manager to a database, which every part of the program uses instead of creating its own.

items: Singleton: an object is created once and shared everywhere, like one key to a special room.
